gloss: to come apart at the seams; to begin to bloom; to break into a smile

forms.label: Past polite
forms.negative: ほころびませんでした

forms.label: ている past
forms.negative: ほころんでいなかった

forms.label: ている past polite
forms.negative: ほころんでいませんでした

definitions.gloss: to come apart at the seams; to come undone; to rip open
definitions.explanation: Stitching or fabric begins to split open or unravel. The original, literal meaning of the word.

definitions.gloss: to begin to bloom; to start to open (of flower buds)
definitions.explanation: Flower buds begin to open, showing the first signs of blooming. A poetic and commonly used sense.

definitions.gloss: to break into a smile; to soften (of one's expression)
definitions.explanation: A face or expression relaxes and a smile naturally emerges. Often used for a gentle, involuntary smile.

examples.japanese: コートの{縫|ぬ}い{目|め}がほころんだ。
examples.english: The seam of the coat came apart.

examples.japanese: {古|ふる}い{着物|きもの}の{袖|そで}がほころびていた。
examples.english: The sleeve of the old kimono was coming undone.

examples.japanese: {長|なが}く{着|き}すぎて、あちこちほころびてしまった。
examples.english: I wore it for so long that it started coming apart all over.

examples.japanese: {梅|うめ}の{蕾|つぼみ}がほころび{始|はじ}めた。
examples.english: The plum buds have started to open.

examples.japanese: {庭|にわ}の{桜|さくら}がほころぶ{季節|きせつ}になった。
examples.english: The season has come when the garden's cherry blossoms begin to bloom.

examples.japanese: {春|はる}の{日差|ひざ}しを{受|う}けて、{花|はな}がほころんでいた。
examples.english: The flowers were opening up in the spring sunshine.

examples.japanese: {思|おも}わず{顔|かお}がほころんだ。
examples.english: A smile involuntarily spread across my face.

examples.japanese: {赤|あか}ちゃんを{見|み}て、みんなの{表情|ひょうじょう}がほころんだ。
examples.english: Everyone's expression softened when they saw the baby.

examples.japanese: {合格|ごうかく}の{知|し}らせを{聞|き}いて、{母|はは}の{顔|かお}がほころんだ。
examples.english: My mother's face broke into a smile when she heard the news of my passing.

notes:
A beautiful word that connects three meanings through the image of something gently opening: seams splitting, buds blooming, and faces softening into smiles. Can also be written {綻|ほころ}ぶ in kanji, though hiragana is more common.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {顔|かお}がほころぶ — to break into a smile
- {蕾|つぼみ}がほころぶ — buds begin to open
- {縫|ぬ}い{目|め}がほころぶ — a seam comes apart
- {表情|ひょうじょう}がほころぶ — one's expression softens

USAGE:
Senses 2 and 3 are the most common in modern Japanese. The word has a gentle, poetic quality. Sense 3 specifically describes a natural, involuntary smile — not a deliberate grin. Often used with {思|おも}わず (involuntarily).

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {咲|さ}く — to bloom (more general; ほころぶ emphasizes the very beginning of blooming)
- ほほえむ — to smile (neutral; ほころぶ emphasizes the involuntary, natural quality of the smile)
